newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Egypt peace envoy to resume Israel, PLO mediation.
newsitem.headline: Egypt peace envoy to resume Israel, PLO mediation.

text.p: Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak's envoy Osama el-Baz will resume a mediation bid between Israel and the Palestinian Authority next week, Egypt's ambassador to Israel said on Wednesday.
"He will come back next week after we consult with the parties concerned to find a suitable agenda," Ambassador Mohammad Bassiouny told Israel's Army radio.
Egypt stepped up its mediation efforts after the United States failed to defuse a crisis over Israel's start of work on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March.
Baz's shuttle diplomacy between Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat has so far failed to achieve a breakthrough.
"Now he (Baz) is dealing with the main issues, not procedures," Bassiouny said.
Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said in Jordan on Tuesday Arab-Israeli peace negotiations had reached their lowest point in 20 years.
"We have to be optimistic. But I am not," Moussa said.
The three-month-old deadlock in peace moves has been punctuated by outbursts of violent clashes between Palestinian demonstrators and Israeli troops.

Moussa reiterated that Israel must suspend all settlement building on Arab land before progress could be made. Israel, which says it has the right to build on lands it captured in the 1967 Middle East war, rejects the demand.
Netanyahu says Arafat must crack down on militants and restore security cooperation with the Jewish state before talks can resume.

The Palestinians see the East Jerusalem settlement as an Israeli bid to preempt final status peace talks on the fate of the city, which Palestinians want to be the capital of a future state. Israel regards East Jerusalem as part of its capital.
